alignments.note: One adverb rendered by the supplied frame *in … manner*; the head is *like*, the word carrying the lexeme's similarity sense, *manner* being the frame's generic completion exactly as rule 99 treats *manner of*. Corrected at reconciliation from *manner*: the corpus heads this English string on *like* in ten of its thirteen units and on *manner* in three, and heads this same lemma on *like* at 1TI.5.25. A head on *manner* remains defensible and is what LUK.22.20 and MRK.14.31 took, both conceding *like* in their own notes.
Verbless clause with an adjectival predicate: the supplied *must be* is a rule 53 helper on the adjective, and rule 11 keeps the ASV's italics from making it `added`.
Compound adjective rendered by a compound; head on the governing element *tongued*.

Bare dative with no determiner: the case preposition *to* rides with the noun under rule 21's determinerless clause, discontinuously under rule 15. Reading *given to* as one phrasal unit on the participle is the competing analysis, refused because rule 36 keeps a governing English preposition off the verb.

One compound adjective rendered *greedy of filthy lucre*: *filthy* glosses αἰσχρο- and *lucre* κερδ-, while *greedy of* is the supplied frame answering to neither element separately, so rule 17 heads on the compound's own head element, *lucre*. This is the reading 1TI.3.2's φιλόξενον → *given to hospitality* takes, heading on the glossed element as TIT.1.8 and 1PE.4.9 do. TIT.1.7 heads this identical English on *greedy*, in the corpus's one other unit of this lemma and with no head reasoning recorded; that reading remains defensible and the divergence is entered in the chapter's conventions.
